Quality control of the optimizer

Source: vignettes/articles/quality-control.qmd

This page records how the native engine’s optimizer is tested and where its technical decisions are written down. The two tables below are generated from the repository files at site build (tests/sim/gates.csv, tests/sim/structures.csv and the front matter of planning/specs/ADR-*.md), so they cannot drift from them. Plan and ledger: planning/specs/BRAINSTORM-optimizer-quality-control-2026-10-23.md. The model syntax for the external oracles (lavaan, OpenMx, and semopy) is on One model in medfit, lavaan, OpenMx and semopy.

Principles

  • Every number has an independent oracle (lavaan, OpenMx, OLS, a hand calculation or a known truth).
  • Every gate has a planted defect it must catch, and the driver plants defects in every gate’s results.
  • An unresolved result beats a wrong one: a refit or a branch that cannot be fitted is reported as unresolved or stops the fit; it is never replaced by the best of the others.
  • Evidence is designed before it is run: the gate’s thresholds and design are committed first.

A token in Planted defects is a MUTANT= value of the gate’s script; the driver (tests/sim/run-gates.R --mutants) also plants tolerance, missing, failed, unreadable and stale results in every gate. test-gate-coverage.R fails when a row has no oracle, names a defect its script does not contain, or when a structure has no gate.

Evidence validators

A native fit carries an outcome ledger (fit@diagnostics$ledger, since 0.14.1): the restriction, the sample, the optimizer’s acceptance state, the discrepancy and the notices, one node per zero-product branch. The ledger is evidence, and the code that decides whether evidence is accepted is itself a QC subject: a false acceptance passes a forged or mismatched fit, and a false refusal turns a genuine result into an error. mbco_sem() runs the validators twice, on the ledger of the fit it is given and on its own root ledger before it returns. A refusal is the error medfit_error_ledger, a class that is never an optimizer failure and never becomes an unresolved row. The semantics of the ledger are in the troubleshooting guide; the decisions are ADR D-11 and D-12.

What the validators accept and refuse. A node is accepted only when what it must contain can be rebuilt from its own constraints and the call: the child count and branch map, the IDs and parents, the shared sample (by digest), domain and settings, the minimum over the resolved branches, and, for a certified-empty branch, the premises of its certificate. A forged ID, count, state, digest, certificate or dropped child is refused. The MBCO root additionally ties each null to the returned $tests table and to the settings its refit used.

Nonzero-product coverage has a separate validator. The optional internal search_evidence record does not alter the version-1 ledger. Its validator rebuilds supported-shape classification and sign bounds from the canonical model, checks the sample/settings context, exact parameter coordinates, candidate objectives, acceptance gates and actual attempt counts, and refuses fabricated local coverage or false emptiness. The independent tests use a separately parameterized likelihood and covariance calculation, plus forged-record and removed-validator defects (test-sem-nonzero-branches.R, test-sem-nonzero-evidence.R). Covered sign domains do not establish global optimality; see Computation and algorithms.

Genuine shapes must validate. A validator is also tested the other way: every shape mbco_sem() can produce must pass it. The shapes of a null node are:

Shape Arises when Evidence in the suite
plain resolved an ordinary refit with a == 0 test-sem-mbco-root.R
resolved zero-product union the null holds a zero-product row and its branches resolve test-sem-mbco-root-qa.R
covariance-retained the refit’s optimizer accepted and covariance explicitly diagnosed non-positive-definite information or a negative variance (warning, covariance = "failed"); arbitrary covariance errors propagate test-sem-post-fit.R, test-sem-mbco-root.R, test-sem-covariance-diagnostic.R
covariance-failed branch in a union one branch of a union lost its covariance; the node reports the first such branch test-sem-post-fit.R, test-sem-mbco-root-qa.R
certified excluded the null contradicts the fit’s own literal equalities test-sem-mbco-root.R
union with an excluded branch a certified-empty branch beside a resolved one test-sem-literal-certificates.R
all-excluded union every branch certified empty: unresolved, no likelihood test-sem-mbco-root.R, test-sem-literal-certificates.R
failed with the engine’s ledger the refit stopped with an error that carries its own ledger test-sem-mbco-root.R
failed bare node the refit stopped with no ledger, so mbco_sem() builds the node: no likelihood, no witness, the condition test-sem-mbco-root.R
failed union with a failed branch a union where at least one branch is unresolved and the others are resolved or excluded test-sem-mbco-root.R
latent a model with a latent mediator, through the same path test-sem-mbco.R

test-sem-mbco-root-qa.R adds the grid of genuine calls (plain, k paths, inequality, equality, boundary, fixed_x both ways, mean structure, expected information, n_starts and control overrides) and the sandwich fit.

What is deliberately not decided. Some forgeries cannot be told from a genuine result without refitting, and the validator does not claim to catch them: a consistent rewrite of the root sample together with every sample_hash, and an altered parameter value inside the parameter table of a null. The free text of the condition of a failed null (message, class and call) is not checked. An all-excluded null is validated against its own certificates only, so a foreign self-consistent all-excluded union is accepted; the statistic is NA either way, so no number changes.

Adding a model

A change that alters the objective, the parameter vector, the constraint set, the bounds or the solver path (the files in tests/sim/risk-files.txt) is high-risk, and its pull request body carries this checklist, each item ticked or n/a: <reason> (the risk-tier workflow checks it). Every new model class needs at least items 1 to 3.

# Check Evidence
1 Independent oracle lavaan, OpenMx, OLS or a hand calculation agrees within a stated tolerance
2 Reliability cell the structure is in the reliability grid (default and random starts, the data scales)
3 Planted defect a mutant the gate must reject
4 Metamorphic invariance rescaling a variable, reordering syntax, or a redundant constraint leaves the answer unchanged
5 Fault injection bad solver statuses and non-finite values are refused or retried, never accepted
6 Registration a gates.csv row with oracle and mutants, and a row in structures.csv
7 Platform run the gate passes on the OpenBLAS runner

The monthly run

The monthly-only semopy gate compares estimates and standard errors for observed, latent, parallel and serial models. A comparison counts only when semopy also agrees with lavaan. The gate uses semopy 2.3.11 and requires uv in the monthly workflow; outside that workflow an unavailable dependency produces n/a rows. semopy and medfit both use SLSQP, so lavaan provides a separate solver check.

The qc-monthly workflow runs the gates on dev on the first of each month, appends one row to a history on the qc-results branch (the environment fingerprint, one PASS or FAIL per gate, the largest restoration ratio, the reliability match rate, the oracle-sweep outcomes), and opens one deduplicated GitHub issue when a gate fails or the R version, BLAS library, nloptr, lavaan or OpenMx version changes. The runner image is recorded and never alerts. Drift bands are not set yet: they need about eight rows (eight months at this cadence; a manual run adds one sooner), and a change merged to dev can go unseen for up to a month unless a run is started by hand or a pull request carries the run-qc label. A labeled pull-request run verifies that pull request; it does not append a scheduled/manual history row. The exact source and run must be checked before reusing either kind of evidence.

Known limits

  • No latent-model solver benchmark exists; the solver decisions that depend on one are marked proposed in the decision log.
  • Gates run on the runner’s OpenBLAS; the reference BLAS needs a separate container.
  • The constrained covariance tests include multiple seeds and extreme variance scales, but do not exhaust boundary optima or establish boundary calibration. The extreme-floor observed sandwich oracle reached a normalized discrepancy of 1.39e-4; this is a numerical limit of that fixture, not a general accuracy guarantee.
  • The evidence validators are not a gate: R/sem-outcomes.R and R/sem-mbco.R are not in tests/sim/risk-files.txt and no gates.csv row registers them, so their protection is the unit tests and the admission checklist, not the OpenBLAS gate run.
  • The validators cannot detect a consistent rewrite of the root sample and its hashes, an altered parameter value inside the parameter table of a null, or a changed condition text of a failed null (see Evidence validators).
  • An all-excluded null is validated against its own certificates, not against the fit’s model, so a self-consistent foreign union is accepted (the statistic is NA regardless).
  • A complete enumeration of zero-product branches is not a global-optimum certificate, and a ledger records what a fit did, not that its optimum is the global one.

The 0.15.0 defaults flip

0.15.0 changes two defaults of the native engine: an unset fixed_x fixes the exogenous observed variables and an unset meanstructure is TRUE. The release is gated on evidence that the change moves only what it should. It moves the conditional log likelihood, the parameter count behind AIC and BIC, the names in coef(), and the retry seed; structural estimates and their standard errors stay where they were.

Gate What it shows
Oracle matrix (tests/sim/native-defaults-oracle.R) 557 rows comparing the default fit with the 0.14.x settings and with lavaan: 503 pass, 54 limit, 0 block
lavaan fixed.x = TRUE, meanstructure = TRUE the default fit has the same row set, parameter count and conditional log likelihood, with coefficients within 1e-15 and standard errors within 2.1e-11
Planted defects a resolver that overwrites an explicit FALSE, or leaves the old default in fit_mediation() only, is caught by the tests; restoring the old default fails nine of the twelve rewritten test files (the other three pin explicit settings)
Full suite 1694 tests, 8580 expectations, 0 failed (reference BLAS)

A documented limit. compare_lr() with lavaan can put the product-null likelihood ratio above the reference (issue #320): 18 of 60 runs for lavaan and 13 of 60 for OpenMx, on the pinned design and seeds. The 2026-10-26 re-measure reproduced both counts on the v0.14.0 tree and on dev, so the flip does not change them, and the limit is documented in ?compare_lr.

At that local checkpoint. The two OpenBLAS gate runs (gates (rest) and gates (reliability)) run on pull requests to main; they were deferred to the release pull request. The table above records the local checkpoint, not a later hosted run. The record, with its sources, is planning/specs/RESULT-qc-0.15.0-native-defaults-flip-2026-10-26.md.

D4 constrained covariance verification

PR #358 added Lagrangian observed curvature, preserved expected Fisher semantics, and projected the corresponding sandwich bread with case-score meat. Independent likelihood parameterizations, Fisher and case-score calculations check these choices; the regression cases cover weights, means, inactive inequalities, active bounds, exact pinned zeros and singular tangent information. See the Methods article for the formulas and boundary limitations.

Receipt Source and scope
Hosted OpenBLAS QC cf7cfb4: 24 gates and 155 checks, including 76,800 reliability fits and 350 semopy comparisons; this run predates the later test-only heads
Hosted coverage dc575a11: 96.38% overall and 97.82% patch coverage; both targeted covariance edge branches were covered

These receipts identify what ran at each source revision. They do not claim 100% coverage of critical paths or a later rerun of the OpenBLAS matrix. Development pull requests keep fast Ubuntu coverage, lint, risk-tier and pkgdown checks. The expensive OpenBLAS runs and full platform matrix are reserved for release pull requests from dev to main; monthly and manual QC remain available.

Lessons from the 0.14.1 port

The recurring defect of the ledger port was the false refusal of a genuine result, not the acceptance of a forgery: a sandwich fit refused because its nulls are refit model-based while the root records the sandwich setting, and an all-excluded zero-product null refused as malformed. Each was found by the full suite or an adversarial reviewer and missed by the hand-built grids, which tested the shapes their authors had thought of. The rule that came out of it is the table above: list every shape the engine can produce and require each to validate, then run the whole suite, since the engine reaches shapes no grid enumerates.

Two process notes. Coverage instrumentation rewrites function bodies, so a mutant that replaces source text in a function cannot find it under covr; those mutants skip under coverage and run in every other check. And the review that found the MBCO root ledger without a validator was an adversarial review, a reader independent of the slice’s own QA, looking for what the author’s tests assume. The record of the release is planning/specs/RESULT-qc-0.14.1-d1-d4-2026-10-25.md.
